note: Curated waypoint descriptions, keyed by the stable ids in data/waypoint-ids.json. Applied by scripts/build-trails.ts (overriding any description from the GPX source) and uploadable to the comments API with scripts/upload-descriptions.ts. Listed east to west, from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves, matching the km order of the generated trail data. Mount George has no entry: no source described it beyond a signpost. Sources for each fact: plans/waypoint-description-sources.md.

descriptions.name: Pulpit Hill
descriptions.description: The hill at the Katoomba end of the track, on whose side stands the Explorers Tree, where Blaxland, Wentworth and Lawson are said to have carved their names on their 1813 crossing of the mountains. The tree is long dead; it was caged in 1884 to protect the carvings, which can no longer be seen.

descriptions.name: Katoomba (2 km east)
descriptions.description: Start of the track near the Explorers Tree on Pulpit Hill Road, about 2 km west of Katoomba, with parking at the Explorers Tree. Katoomba has supermarkets, shops and the railway station. The track follows an 1884 horse track to Jenolan Caves, named for its width.

descriptions.name: Six Foot Track Information Shelter
descriptions.description: Dirt car park and shelter with a large Six Foot Track information sign, about 260 m from the Explorers Tree.

descriptions.name: Norths Lookout
descriptions.description: Fenced lookout a short side trip off the track, with views over Nellies Glen and into the Megalong Valley. Below it the track drops steeply down the Nellies Glen steps, between tall rock walls and back and forth across a small creek.

descriptions.name: Therabulat Lookout
descriptions.description: Clifftop lookout, also spelled Therabalut, with views over the Megalong Valley.

descriptions.name: Old Ford Reserve
descriptions.description: Roadside campground a few metres north of the Megalong Road bridge over Megalong Creek, reached by car, with a wheelchair-accessible toilet, flat tent space and access to the creek. Being beside the road, it can be noisy at times.

descriptions.name: Coxs River Camp Area
descriptions.description: Grassy campground on the western bank of the Coxs River, with a toilet, a sheltered picnic table and good river access; it is a fuel-stove-only area. Water comes from a rainwater tank or the river, neither of them treated. The river is normally shin-deep at the crossing; when it floods, Bowtells Swing Bridge, built by the Royal Australian Engineers in 1992, is the way across.

descriptions.name: Alum Creek Campground
descriptions.description: The least used and least developed of the track's campgrounds, in a sheltered gully beside the small Alum Creek; NSW National Parks lists no toilet here. Water can normally be collected from Alum Creek and the fairly reliable Little River down the road, except in prolonged dry periods. From here the track climbs the Black Range on a dirt road, with no further water until the Black Range tank.

descriptions.name: Black Range Camp Ground
descriptions.description: Campground on the Black Range, also reachable by car, with toilets, a covered picnic table and an information board with a map; it is a fuel-stove-only area. The rainwater tank is fairly reliable but has run empty in long dry spells and through vandalism, and the water is untreated.

descriptions.name: Jenolan Caves
descriptions.description: The end of the track, reached by a steep, rocky descent along a narrow ridge with views down to the Blue Lake. The cave system dates back at least 340 million years; the heritage-listed Caves House, built in 1898, has dining, accommodation and a shop selling essentials.
